variants: Galbot's developer platform lists the G1 and a G1 Lite as compatible robots; its G1 page lists end effectors swappable between dexterous hands, suction cups and grippers. This record covers the G1 page.
availability_note: Galbot's G1 page has a Buy Now button that opens a JD.com product page, a third-party retailer the record does not cite, and a Contact Us button. The page states no price and no delivery time.

named_models.name: AstraBrain-WAM
named_models.role_note: Galbot's home page says "AstraBrain-WAM is a general-purpose cerebrum model that unlocks the value of diverse data at global scale." Its architecture diagram labels the cerebrum a 3B-13B World Action Model that interprets task semantics, plans long-horizon tasks and issues high-level commands.

named_models.name: AstraBrain-WBC
named_models.role_note: Galbot's home page says "AstraBrain-WBC is the world's first general-purpose humanoid cerebellum GPT foundation model." Its architecture diagram labels the cerebellum an 80-300M Transformer that does real-time control and whole-body and whole-hand control.

named_models.name: AstraBrain-Dex
named_models.role_note: Galbot's home page says "AstraBrain-Dex is a world model that enables robots to perform high-precision in-hand manipulation with unprecedented dexterity."

hardware.compute: An NVIDIA AGX Orin 64GB computing platform rated at 275 TOPS, with Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz and Bluetooth 5.2.
hardware.sensors: A binocular camera in the head, four RGB cameras and an IMU in the torso, two depth cameras and two 6-axis force sensors at the wrists, and a 3D LiDAR, eight ultrasonic sensors and an IMU in the chassis. A 5.5-inch touchscreen, two linear 4-microphone arrays and two 5 W speakers are listed.
hardware.actuation: 21 degrees of freedom excluding the chassis and end effector, 2 in the neck, 7 in each arm, 3 in the waist and 2 in the legs, with a payload of 5 kg per arm and 10 kg in total, a 4-wheel omnidirectional chassis and a maximum speed of 1.5 m/s. The page states a height of up to 1730 mm and a weight of 92.5 kg.
hardware.power: A 48 V, 30 Ah battery with an 8-hour operating time and 3.5-hour adapter charging, and an IP54 ingress protection rating.

developer_access: Galbot's developer platform describes GalbotSDK with a high-level API that invokes the robot's built-in planning, navigation and whole-body control algorithms and a low-level API that directly controls joint motors, sets chassis velocity and reads raw sensor streams, and it lists the Control domain as "High-precision, low-latency actuator control with end-to-end model action passthrough". The platform adds an online simulation, one-click deployment from the platform to a real robot, and standard G1 and S1 digital models in URDF, MJCF and USD. A free developer tier lists GalbotSDK, the docs center and the digital models.
terms_note: Galbot's Terms of Use apply to the Galbot website and say it may be used for informational purposes only; that is a site notice, not terms of sale or software terms, and it is not classified. The G1 page and developer platform were read at review time and no terms of sale, SDK licence or warranty page was found on either.
not_verified: The named models and the documented SDK route are Galbot's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Galbot web page that Galbot can change at any time, and the pages are bilingual, with the English text a rendered translation of the Chinese source.
